title: Vector Databases & High-Dimensional Indexing
description: Master vector database architectures, HNSW vs IVFFlat indexing, distance metrics, and integration with Azure AI Search and Qdrant in .NET.

data.text: How Vector Databases Work Under the Hood

Relational databases index scalar values (numbers, strings) using B-Trees to provide O(log N) lookups for equality and ranges. However, embeddings are dense vectors residing in high-dimensional vector spaces (such as 1536 dimensions for text-embedding-3-small). Performing brute-force cosine distance calculations against 10 million vectors requires scanning every vector (O(N) complexity), resulting in unacceptable latency.

Vector databases solve this using Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) search algorithms. Rather than guaranteeing the absolute closest point, ANN algorithms navigate graph or cluster indexes to return points with 95%+ recall in single-digit milliseconds.

cards.title: Cosine Similarity
cards.description: Measures the cosine of the angle between two vectors, ignoring magnitude. Ideal for text embeddings where document length variations should not skew semantic similarity.

cards.title: Dot Product (Inner Product)
cards.description: Calculates the sum of products of corresponding vector components. When vectors are pre-normalized to unit length (L2 norm = 1.0), Dot Product is mathematically identical to Cosine Similarity but computes 3x faster.

cards.title: Euclidean Distance (L2)
cards.description: Calculates the straight-line geometric distance between two points in space. Highly sensitive to vector magnitude.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Vector databases use ANN algorithms (like HNSW) to search millions of vectors in sub-5ms latency
HNSW offers the best query speed and recall balance at the cost of higher memory consumption
Use Cosine Similarity or normalized Dot Product for text embeddings
Combine payload metadata filtering with vector similarity to partition enterprise data by tenant or department
Apply scalar quantization (SQ) when scaling beyond tens of millions of vectors to cut RAM costs in half
data.takeaway: Understanding vector indexing and distance metrics is vital for sizing, scaling, and maintaining high-throughput semantic search backends in .NET enterprise architectures.
